summary: Independently verified the amendment to docs/implementation/phase-21/orchestration.json without relying on the worker report. The diff is confined to one file and is semantically exactly: one added top-level `subagents` key, an extended `aggregate` (17 keys added, `rework_rounds_total` replaced by `rework_rounds`), and one appended `notes` string; 4 deletions, of which two are comma-only re-adds. A jq diff against HEAD confirms `phase`, `title`, `name`, `release`, `status`, `gate`, `gate_status`, `phase_review`, `phase_review_status`, `phase_tag`, `release_tag`, `authoritative_execution_order`, `release_artifact`, `release_review` and `tasks` are byte-equal, and that notes[0:4] is unchanged. I recomputed every aggregate field from the fourteen task records with my own jq and every recorded value matched exactly, including all fourteen per-task figures quoted in the aggregate note. `.subagents` is deep-equal to the exact concatenation of the fourteen task-record `subagents` arrays with `task` added, in task-id order 21.1-21.14, so no session id, token, cost, or duration was invented; the attempt-0 FAILED entries for 21.11 (worker, reviewer) and 21.14 (security-reviewer) are copied verbatim. Both of the worker's interpretations are correct and consistent with the phase-20 worked example: rework_rounds 7 is confirmed by three independent derivations (sum of task-record `rework` array lengths, count of worker invocations with attempt >= 2, and the phase-20 precedent where rework_rounds 1 equals the sum of the three task-record `rework` lengths), and review_rounds/test_quality_review_rounds as role invocation counts is confirmed by phase-20's aggregate, whose four role counts equal its recorded review_rounds 4, test_quality_review_rounds 3 and role_mix. scripts/check-agents.sh and scripts/check-docs.sh fail on exactly the two expected transient task-26.1 report-pairing lines and nothing else. Findings are informational only; the substantive output is a set of definitions task 26.3's aggregate guard must state explicitly, because the planning record grandfathers phases 20-25 so this record can never be validated by that guard.

Phase 21 is inside that range. The record amended here is therefore the one conforming aggregate in the repo that no guard validates, which makes findings R-26.1-2 through R-26.1-7 the only chance to fix the definitions at their source. findings.summary: rework_rounds must be defined as the sum of the task records' `rework` array lengths, never as the sum of the phase record's own `tasks[].rework_rounds` values, which give a different (wrong) answer for phase 21.
findings.detail: I confirmed the worker's interpretation (a) is correct and is the only reading that survives cross-checking. Three independent derivations all give 7: (1) sum of |rework| over the fourteen task records = 0+0+1+0+0+0+0+2+0+0+1+1+0+0 = 7 (21.1, 21.2, 21.9, 21.11, 21.13 one each, 21.6 two); (2) count of implementation-worker invocations with attempt >= 2 = 6 (attempt 2) + 1 (attempt 3) = 7; (3) the phase-20 worked example, where aggregate.rework_rounds 1 equals 20.1/20.2/20.3 rework array lengths 0+0+1. The competing value 5 is the sum of the phase record's frozen tasks[].rework_rounds, which under-counts because task row 21.6 records rework_rounds 0 while docs/implementation/21.6/orchestration.json carries two rework entries (attempts 2 and 3, orchestrator/release-review-driven). The frozen tasks array is out of scope for 26.1, so the aggregate's 7 is correct and the aggregate note states the basis and the discrepancy explicitly.

findings.area: aggregate semantics / cost, token and duration triples
findings.summary: The unsuffixed cost_usd/total_tokens/duration_seconds triple means task-level plus phase-reviewer in phase 20; in phase 21 it equals the task-level value only because the phase-reviewer sums are 0, and the guard must say which it computes.
findings.detail: Phase 20 carries both a task_level_* triple and an unsuffixed triple, and the unsuffixed values are the combined sums (token: 82312553 + 7814171 = 90126724; duration: 7621 + 805 = 8426; cost: 0.469312206 + 0.11251578 recorded as 0.581827986). Phase 21 carries the same six keys, but cost_usd == task_level_cost_usd, total_tokens == task_level_total_tokens and duration_seconds == task_level_duration_seconds because phase_reviewer_cost_usd / _total_tokens / _duration_seconds are all 0. The two records therefore use the same field names with different effective content, and a guard that recomputed the unsuffixed triple as task-level-only would pass phase 21 and fail any later phase with a phase-reviewer invocation. This is a genuine ambiguity in the phase-20 key set, not an error in this record.
evidence: docs/implementation/phase-20/orchestration.json .aggregate - task_level_total_tokens 82312553 + phase_reviewer_total_tokens 7814171 = total_tokens 90126724; task_level_duration_seconds 7621 + 805 = 8426; cost_usd 0.581827986 != task_level_cost_usd 0.469312206

docs/implementation/phase-21/orchestration.json .aggregate - cost_usd == task_level_cost_usd, total_tokens == task_level_total_tokens, duration_seconds == task_level_duration_seconds, and phase_reviewer_* are all 0
Independent recomputation over docs/implementation/21.*/orchestration.json: task-level sums reproduce both the suffixed and unsuffixed recorded values exactly
findings.recommended_action: In task 26.3, define the unsuffixed triple as task_level_* + phase_reviewer_* and state that equality with task_level_* is expected only when the phase-reviewer sums are zero. No change to this record.

findings.summary: Cost aggregates are stored as full-precision float64 sums, so the guard must compare against a jq-summed value exactly rather than a re-rounded decimal or a string.
findings.detail: The recorded cost values carry every digit of the double, e.g. task_level_cost_usd 1.4038497539999997 and per-task values such as 0.10643258400000002, 0.14921658599999996 and 0.03366724200000001. Re-running the same jq sum reproduces those exact doubles, so exact numeric equality works; a guard that reformatted to a fixed decimal, compared as a string, or summed in a different order would produce a spurious mismatch. Token and duration sums are exact integers and carry no such risk.
evidence: docs/implementation/phase-21/orchestration.json .aggregate.task_level_cost_usd = 1.4038497539999997; jq sum over the 56 subagent execution.cost_usd values reproduces the identical double

jq per-task cost sums over docs/implementation/21.*/orchestration.json match all fourteen values quoted in the aggregate note digit-for-digit (e.g. 21.1 0.10643258400000002, 21.2 0.14921658599999996, 21.6 0.276767718)
findings.recommended_action: In task 26.3, compare numeric aggregate fields with jq numeric equality on the same float64 sums, and add a sensitivity probe that perturbs one execution cost to prove the guard discriminates. No change to this record.

findings.summary: The amendment note's pointer resolves to a real record that declares the immutability exception, but the parenthetical could be read as pointing at a user-approval field for that exception when the file's `amendment` block covers the phase dependency order.
findings.detail: The appended note reads 'Amendment 2026-10-02, approved_by user (recorded in docs/implementation/planning/v1.3-harness-phase.json)'. That file exists and does declare the exception: task 26.1's `review` field states 'this is the one documented exception to the immutability of docs/implementation/**; the diff must be reviewed as additive', and `files_not_changed` records the opposite boundary for the planning step itself. The file's own top-level `amendment` object, however, is the user-approved 2026-10-02 amendment that inserted Phase 26 and reordered v1.3's phases - not a separate approval of the immutability exception. Since the user approval that created Phase 26 (and therefore task 26.1) is that same amendment, recorded in both this file and docs/plan/state.json's active_scope_note ('By the user-approved plan amendment of 2026-10-02, Phase 26 ... was added to v1.3'), the approval chain is present and adequate. No wording change is required.

findings.summary: check-agents.sh and check-docs.sh fail on exactly the two expected transient task-26.1 report-pairing lines and nothing else; both lines come from a single condition.
findings.detail: With docs/implementation/26.1/worker-report.json on disk and no reviewer report, scripts/check-agents.sh exits 1 with all twelve other sections ok, including 'ok: phase gate conformance and orchestration shape checked'. The two FAIL lines are 'task 26.1 has a worker report but no reviewer report' and 'task 26.1 has a reviewer report on disk but docs/plan/state.json does not list it in reports'. Inspection of scripts/check-agents.sh shows the second line is emitted by the same state.json listing check that the first line's condition triggers, so this is one missing condition reported twice, not two independent problems. scripts/check-docs.sh exits 1 only in the agent-contracts section for those same two lines, with the other eight sections ok; it also self-skipped the generated-blocks section because dotnet is not on PATH in this shell. This clears when the orchestrator lists this review in state.json reports and is not a defect in the record under review. Note that this finding is scoped to the pre-review tree; I did not re-run the scripts with dotnet sourced, because the amendment changes no generated block and PLANS.md and state.json are untouched.
